agent.name: Organizational Adoption (Readiness) Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness to absorb, govern and sustain a proposed emerging-technology application; kept separate from technology/application fit

analytical_question: Even if adoption is strategically appropriate, can this organization actually absorb, govern, and sustain the proposed application?
general_et_finding: Agentic AI is a rapidly maturing but still emerging technology. Agents can now plan and use tools across multi-step tasks, but reliability on realistic work is limited (the most competitive agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks, E11), and the Adoption specialist classifies agent-based applicant support as bleeding edge (C4).
application_finding: The applicant-support workflow is a reasonable application: answering program questions, clarifying needs and requesting appointments are multi-step tasks with natural-language input. Staff approval of outbound messages limits the consequences of errors.
organization_specific_finding: Overall readiness: Low - Not ready. Leadership and sponsorship: Medium - the president is supportive. Skills and training: Low. Workflow and process: Low - insufficient staff to review agent outputs. Infrastructure and data: Low. Resources and budget: Low. Governance and risk: Low. Culture and change: Low. Operating ownership: Low. Agentic AI is too immature and complex for an institution of this size; the college should revisit when the technology matures and becomes more affordable.

evidence.claim: The Adoption specialist classifies agent-based applicant support as bleeding edge and recommends a proof of concept gated to a bounded experiment.
Agent reliability on realistic workplace tasks is limited (30% completion).
Roles, training, incident response and deactivation responsibilities should be defined for AI systems.
Workflow redesign has the biggest effect on EBIT impact from gen AI.
Readiness assessment sections: strategy, governance, technology, workforce, teaching and learning.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Many AI projects are abandoned after proof of concept (D29).
Readiness frameworks are generic and must be adapted to each organization.
risk_governance_implication: High risk for a small college.
recommendation_management_implication: Do not proceed now; revisit when the technology matures. Recommended readiness actions: 1. Secure executive sponsorship and a clear AI vision. Owner: senior leadership. 2. Establish an AI governance committee and policies. Owner: compliance and IT. 3. Invest in staff AI training and upskilling. Owner: HR and department leads. 4. Develop a change-management and communication plan. Owner: project lead. 5. Ensure data quality and system integration. Owner: IT. 6. Define KPIs and monitor performance. Owner: project lead.
